title: No demonstrated cross-cohort CRP prediction gain from a low-eosinophil hinge beyond flexible leukocyte measures
abstract: We tested whether max(1-eosinophil percent,0) improves prediction of log C-reactive protein beyond flexible demographic, adiposity, smoking, white-cell differential and neutrophil-to-lymphocyte measures. Ridge spline models trained in 4087 NHANES2005–2006 adults were frozen for 5175 different NHANES2007–2008 adults. MEC-weighted MSE was 1.133310 without and 1.133362 with the hinge; gain was -0.000052 (500 source-refit/target-resample rescaled PSU bootstrap95% interval -0.006275 to 0.003880). No incremental benefit was demonstrated. This narrowly negative representation test does not exclude eosinophil–inflammation associations or small gains. Cohorts share a survey population and protocol, and CBC instruments changed; this is not independent-system clinical validation.
